shared_context.content: For a nonnegative integer n, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j), with the empty product (q;q)_0 := 1.
shared_context.label: finite_q_factorial

shared_context.content: For a positive integer d, Phi_d(q) denotes the d-th cyclotomic polynomial in Z[q].
shared_context.label: cyclotomic_polynomial

shared_context.content: A polynomial F(q) = sum_{j=0}^D c_j q^j is reciprocal of degree D if q^D F(q^{-1}) = F(q), equivalently c_j = c_{D-j} for all 0 <= j <= D.
shared_context.label: reciprocal_polynomial

strategy_summary: Rewrite the product as a balanced two-term q-factorial ratio. Use cyclotomic exponents to get polynomiality from the floor condition. Then separate positivity into an explicit hard bottleneck: prove nonnegativity only for the first half of the coefficients. A simple reciprocity identity for the balanced ratio reflects those coefficients across the midpoint, yielding full coefficientwise nonnegativity.
